kind: live observation (not a reconstruction check): which threads execute the per-step pair update 18b8fa0 and the pair-link worker path, the job dispatcher capacity, and the in-memory shape and state of the objects named by 12 guard globals

capture.mechanism: private bounded plugin, data writes only: (A) the broad-phase object at controller+0x28 had its vtable pointer compare-exchanged to a private copy of the 34-slot table (image RVA 0x29ca8a0) with +0x60/+0x40/+0x88 forwarding detours (S0/S1/S2 inside 18b8fa0); (B) the provider+0x68 pair-collider factory (vtable image RVA 0x29ca780, 4 slots) had its vtable pointer swapped the same way with slot +8 (18de680, a table lookup by the two shape kinds) replaced by a forwarding detour that records the calling thread and return site. No code bytes, page protections or shared .rdata were changed.
capture.identity_checks: image base; 274-byte fingerprint of 18b8fa0 and 64-byte getter fingerprint; all 34 broad-phase slots; controller vtable 0x29ca0e0 from the player body chain; factory vtable pointer equal to image 0x29ca780, its 4 slots and the word before them, a 32-byte fingerprint of 18de680, and the three call-site encodings at 18dda28 / 18e09db / 18e08fb; detours act only for the target object (and, for A, the 18b8fa0 return sites)
capture.lock_reads: at S0, S1 and S2 of up to 48 spaced steps, once inside the worker path of those steps, and every 5 s from the plugin thread: the qword in each guard global and 0x40 bytes at that pointer, via ReadProcessMemory; nothing written
capture.restore: factory then broad-phase vtable pointer compare-exchanged back after re-checking provider+0x68 / controller+0x28; in-flight detours drained; module pinned

reference_shapes_under_wine: a fixture in the same prefix: InitializeCriticalSection gives DebugInfo all-ones, LockCount -1; when held LockCount 0, RecursionCount 1, OwningThread = thread id; SRWLOCK free 0, exclusive 0x10001, shared 0x10000

attempts.outcome: startup navigation stalled on the title screen (budget exhausted) before the plugin was armed; no hook installed; cleanup verified (bottle stopped, saves and settings restored, original DLL verified)

armed and installed (both hooks), with steering holds; about 3.6 min later the launcher watchdog stopped the bottle for host memory pressure (system free memory 19 percent; game RSS about 1.1 GiB), so the process ended with the hooks installed and the in-memory step records were lost; cleanup verified (bottle stopped, saves and settings restored, original DLL verified). Only the install-time thread census survived; it is not analysed.

conclusions.pair_update_thread: not fixed: 18b8fa0 ran on several job-pool threads (one shared start address in the game image) and switched threads between consecutive steps; never on the host plugin thread or the census thread
conclusions.worker_thread: in every recorded step the worker path ran on exactly one thread, the same thread that ran that step
conclusions.dispatcher_capacity: always 1, so the pair-job worker count was 1 even with up to 83 new pairs
conclusions.guard_objects: 11 of 12 globals point to Wine CRITICAL_SECTION-shaped objects, all free at every sample (never held, owner never set); global RVA 0x333c5e8 holds an all-ones value, not a pointer

limits: Wine (Highball, snow-research bottle) on macOS; thread placement and dispatcher capacity may differ on Windows or with another CPU count.
The dispatcher capacity was 1 in every recorded step, so 18b7ca0 took its single-worker path; multi-worker pair jobs could not be produced by gameplay and no concurrent worker execution was observed.
Lock state was sampled at discrete points (S0/S1/S2, first worker-path factory call, periodic); a lock taken and released between samples is not visible.
Worker-path identity comes from the factory slot +8 call inside 18dd400, the two terrain wrappers and the flagged-neighbor paths; a worker pass that reaches none of these is not attributed.
Thread labels are per session; thread ids, heap addresses and raw bytes are kept private.

Step records are bounded per session (12000 in census-01, about 115 s of 240 s); later steps were counted but not attributed. Records were held in memory until restore, so a session ended externally loses them (census-03).
